Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) is a life-sustaining medical treatment that bypasses the normal digestion process, delivering a complete nutrient mix directly into the bloodstream through a central vein. It is used when the gastrointestinal tract is non- functional or inaccessible.

blocks.text: TPN is a complex "all-in-one" admixture (often called a 3-in-1 or TNA) tailored to a patient’s specific metabolic needs.
Provide energy and prevent muscle wasting
Sodium, potassium, magnesium, calcium, chloride, phosphate
Maintain fluid balance, nerve conduction, and bone health
Promote wound healing and enzyme activity
Provides hydration and serves as nutrient
Control blood glucose, prevent catheter clotting, reduce gastric acid secretion

The dosage for Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) is a highly individualized process.
For adults, it is calculated based on ideal body weight (IBW), while for children, it is based on actual weight in kilograms and their specific developmental stage.

blocks.text: Adult requirements focus on maintaining lean body mass and providing enough energy for metabolic stress without "overfeeding," which can damage the liver.
